name: Corridors of Power: Should America Police the World?
note: Dror Moreh's eight-part series: Kissinger, Powell, Albright, Wolfowitz and others on Iraq, Bosnia, Rwanda, Darfur and Syria, and when America should step in. The 2022 film cut is in the movies row.

name: The Corridors of Power
note: The single-film version of the Corridors of Power series, if you'd rather watch it in one go.

name: The Fog of War
note: Start here. Robert McNamara, Defense Secretary during Vietnam, looks back on the power he used and where he got it wrong. Errol Morris, Oscar winner. English.

name: The Diplomat
note: Richard Holbrooke, who negotiated the end of the Bosnian war at Dayton, told by his son. Pairs with Corridors of Power's Bosnia episodes. English.

name: No End in Sight
note: How the Iraq occupation went wrong, told by the insiders who were there. By Charles Ferguson, who made Inside Job. English.

name: Taxi to the Dark Side
note: Alex Gibney's Oscar winner: the death of an Afghan taxi driver in US custody opens up torture policy in the War on Terror. English.

name: Turning Point: 9/11 and the War on Terror
note: Five parts covering the whole arc, from the roots of al-Qaeda through Afghanistan and Iraq to the 2021 withdrawal. English.

name: The Gatekeepers
note: By Dror Moreh, who made Corridors of Power. Six former heads of Israel's Shin Bet speak frankly about security and occupation. Oscar-nominated. Hebrew with subtitles, so not one for dinner.

name: L'abécédaire de Gilles Deleuze
note: Start here. Eight hours of Deleuze talking with Claire Parnet, one letter of the alphabet at a time (A for Animal, D for Desire...). The best way to hear him think; dip in by letter.

name: Monument à Félix Guattari
note: François Pain, who worked with Guattari at La Borde, assembles friends, artists and analysts around plenty of Guattari's own footage: schizoanalysis, the three ecologies and the work with Deleuze. The closest thing to a Guattari portrait.

name: Examined Life
note: Good first watch. Philosophers including Žižek, Judith Butler, Cornel West and Avital Ronell (who comes out of deconstruction) talk through their ideas in plain terms while walking around cities.

name: Derrida
note: Follows Derrida at home and on tour. He explains deconstruction, pushes back on the camera, and the film plays with deconstruction itself. Pairs well with his interview book Positions.

name: Human, All Too Human
note: BBC, three hour-long episodes: Nietzsche, Heidegger, Sartre. Clear background for both Land and Derrida. Start with the Nietzsche episode.

name: The Stranger
note: François Ozon's black-and-white adaptation of Camus's novel. Best after reading the book and The Myth of Sisyphus.

name: The Turin Horse
note: Béla Tarr, spun out of the story of Nietzsche collapsing after embracing a beaten horse in Turin. Slow and bleak on purpose: an experience film in the spirit of Zarathustra, not an explanation.

name: Children of Men
note: Mark Fisher opens Capitalist Realism with this film, as a picture of a world that can no longer imagine a different future. Watch it alongside the book.

name: The Pervert's Guide to Ideology
note: Slavoj Žižek analyzes films from inside recreated scenes. Fisher leans heavily on Žižek in Capitalist Realism, so this is useful context, and very entertaining.

name: The Terminator
note: Its time loop, a machine from the future making sure it gets built, mirrors Land's idea of AI and capital arriving from the future. Mark Fisher wrote about the film too. Backdrop for Fanged Noumena.

name: Inside Job
note: The essential one. Oscar-winning, tightly argued, with tough interviews of economists and officials. Goldman features heavily.

name: Panic: The Untold Story of the 2008 Financial Crisis
note: The rescue told by the people who ran it: Bernanke, Paulson, Geithner. Best inside view of the bailout decisions.

name: Abacus: Small Enough to Jail
note: Steve James on the only US bank criminally charged after the crisis: a small family bank in Chinatown. Unrelated to Goldman's Abacus deal.

name: HyperNormalisation
note: Adam Curtis. Traces how finance took power from politicians, starting with New York's 1975 fiscal crisis.

name: Capital in the Twenty-First Century
note: Based on Piketty's book. Archival-collage style close to Adam Curtis.

name: Frontline
note: Watch these episodes: 'Money, Power and Wall Street' (2012, four parts, the most thorough account), 'The Warning' (2009, the failed fight to regulate derivatives) and 'The Untouchables' (2013, why no bankers were prosecuted). For US foreign policy: 'Ghosts of Rwanda' (2004, why the US and UN stood by during the genocide).

name: Meltdown: The Secret History of the Global Collapse
note: CBC, four parts. Global angle: Iceland, Europe and how the contagion spread.

name: All Watched Over by Machines of Loving Grace
note: Adam Curtis. Episode one covers Greenspan, Ayn Rand and the belief that markets stabilize themselves.
